llm.summary: This is a coherent Chinese K12 chemistry lesson-planning skill with scoped classroom data use and clear teacher-review and safety boundaries.

dimensions.detail: It uses local class-workspace data and file/export capability for lesson planning, which is proportionate to the purpose; the schema is scoped to class profile, weakness summaries, tiers, logs, review plans, and pending lesson-plan entries.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown references and a JSON schema only; I found no executable scripts, install hooks, remote payload retrieval, command execution, or dependency installation behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are educational and bounded: generated outputs are drafts for teacher review, experiments are only marked as lesson slots, and crisis or exam-cheating situations route to protective protocols.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill relies on platform memory for a class chemistry dossier, but it discloses view/correct/delete/pause/no-share/export controls, avoids real student names and sensitive personal fields, and states writes are pending until teacher confirmation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill is narrowly framed for chemistry lesson planning, unit compression, curriculum alignment, and draft classroom question chains; it explicitly excludes full lab procedures, exam design, other subjects, and direct student instruction.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, confirm this skill is being used for Chinese-language mainland China K12 chemistry teaching or that the operator has localized curriculum, language, data-consent rules, and crisis contacts for the deployment region. Treat lesson plans and experiment placements as teacher-reviewed drafts, especially where class records or lab safety are involved.
llm.findings:
[AE4] expected: The flagged files are Chinese UTF-8 curriculum materials; byte inspection showed normal text starts and no zero-width or bidirectional control characters, so this appears to be a language/content signal rather than analysis evasion.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-only content is consistent with the declared mainland China Chinese K12 target; shared platform and crisis files state that other regions require localization and region checks before giving emergency channels.
[AIG-SARIF] expected: The static scan reported no T01-T09 results, which matches the artifact review: no code execution, privilege escalation, persistence hooks, tool spoofing, or remote retrieval were present.
